rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for contrasting one clause with another.

example.english: I like iced lemon tea, whereas my friend likes hot milk tea.
example.traditional: 我鍾意飲凍檸茶，但係我朋友鍾意飲熱奶茶。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 ji3 jam2 dung3 ning2 caa4 daan6 hai6 ngo5 pang4 jau5 zung1 ji3 jam2 jit6 naai5 caa4

rows.note: Use this mainly in written or formal comparisons where the two clauses are presented in parallel.

example.english: The elder brother chose to work in Hong Kong, whereas the younger brother plans to emigrate.
example.traditional: 哥哥選擇留港工作，而弟弟則計劃移民外國。
example.jyutping: go1 go1 syun2 zaak6 lau4 gong2 gung1 zok3 ji4 dai6 dai6 zak1 gai3 waak6 ji4 man4 ngoi6 gwok3

rows.note: Use this when the second clause is contrary to what might be expected, rather than merely different.

example.english: I expected the rain to cause a traffic jam, whereas the roads were actually clear all the way.
example.traditional: 我以為落雨會好塞車，反而一路都好順。
